subject.title: [Feature] Prime-number default scheduling for HEARTBEAT / cron “every” + deterministic per-agent phase jitter (anti top-of-hour spikes)

question: Should OpenClaw add public phase, stagger, or prime-cadence controls for cron every schedules, or keep every as a fixed anchored interval and limit anti-herd behavior to heartbeat plus cron expressions?
rationale: The remaining request changes public scheduling semantics, persisted cron shape, CLI/API flags, and docs, and repository policy treats config/default scheduling surfaces as compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Design a narrow cron every phase contract
options.body: Add one explicit cron every scheduling contract with schema, CLI, docs, persistence, and upgrade tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep every fixed
options.body: Preserve the current fixed-anchor `every` semantics and rely on heartbeat phase plus cron-expression stagger for anti-herd behavior.

options.title: Add broader prime mode
options.body: Accept a larger product surface such as prime cadence transforms plus deterministic phase controls for heartbeat and cron, with migration and observability requirements.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow cron every phase contract
recommendation.body: Add one explicit cron every scheduling contract with schema, CLI, docs, persistence, and upgrade tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the existing cron stagger controls and docs, so they are the best history-backed owner for the cron scheduling product boundary.
